elaine: New hire hit a blocker in the Workers quickstart. Deploy fails: `ReferenceError: process is not defined` and later `Uncaught Error: Cannot find module "net"`. The code only calls fetch + jwt verify. Any fast remediation?

hiro: That usually means a transitive dep pulled in Node builtins (buffer/fs/net). Which JWT lib are you using? Some helpers pull in buffer for base64 decoding.

morgan: If you can, switch to a web-first verifier using WebCrypto; avoids node polyfills. Otherwise a small opt-in shim that provides explicit stubs (throws with a clear message) helps.

elaine: We're using jwt-simple; bundle shows `buffer` being pulled in. How do we make esbuild/wrangler stop auto-polyfilling?

hiro: Two options: 1) replace dep with a tiny web-friendly lib, 2) add a conditional `exports` map in the package to expose a worker-specific entrypoint. Example exports pattern: `{"./verify": {"worker":"dist/verify.worker.mjs","node":"dist/verify.node.cjs"}}` so bundlers pick the right file.

morgan: Also set esbuild target `service-worker` or wrangler `compatibility_date` to ensure no node shims. And ensure `define: { 'process.env.NODE_ENV': '"production"' }` isn't causing esbuild to include node runtime helpers.

elaine: WebCrypto also appears different: CF supports crypto.subtle but importKey for spki/raw is flaky in older runtimes. Any guidance?

hiro: Provide a small helper: `importKeyGuard` that checks `typeof crypto?.subtle?.importKey === 'function'` and gives a helpful error with link to docs. If needed, fallback to a WASM verifier or pre-computed JWKS on server side. We recommend calling out the caveat in the sample README.

morgan: Typing and DX: TS projects will hit "cannot find module '@redwood/inference-edge-shims'" unless the shim publishes `index.d.ts`. Add `types` in package.json and a minimal declaration file. Also recommend tsconfig: `{"lib":["es2021","webworker"],"moduleResolution":"bundler","skipLibCheck":true}` for samples.

elaine: CI note: our integration runner failed because tests run in node14 with no WebCrypto. We should run worker-targeted tests in Miniflare.

ci-runner: Created ticket CI-1220 to add a miniflare job and mark worker tests.

hiro: Plan: publish an opt-in `@redwood/inference-edge-shims` with: safeFetchWithAuth (handles single-refresh + backoff), tiny web-crypto guards, and explicit stubs for node builtins that throw a clear error and link to docs. Keep it minimal and ship `.mjs` worker build + `.cjs` node build plus `index.d.ts`.

morgan: We'll also add a devex ESLint rule: if package.json/tsconfig indicates `platform: 'worker'` or `target: 'edge'`, warn on imports from known node modules (`fs`,`net`,`child_process`,`os`,`buffer`). Link suggestions to shim or replacements.

elaine: Great. I'll patch the quickstart to use the shim + web-first verifier and add a short troubleshooting checklist that lists: 1) node builtins, 2) webcrypto caveats, 3) esbuild/wrangler target flags, 4) tsconfig tips. That should cut the onboarding friction.
